A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeInf and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original anomaly-detection comparisons, forecasting data-pruning experiments, model comparisons and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, qualitative scores and RMSE pruning results.

M1.justification: The block-influence calculation, aggregation over overlapping blocks, self/test influence variants and nonparametric extension are retained. Algorithm 1 and Appendix H clarify the existing procedure; the TracIn/Hessian-free terminology change does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The five principal and seven supplementary anomaly datasets, four displayed forecasting datasets and annotation-audit scenarios are retained. Moving forecasting and model-choice studies into appendices and foregrounding existing mislabeled examples adds no new demonstrated task or domain.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 retains v1's four detector baselines and adds TranAD, DCdetector, block LOOCV, conditional influence and LWCV. Figure 7 also labels a Data Shapley comparator in its new RMSE plots, although Appendix E still explicitly excludes that method, leaving its participation inconsistently documented.

E3.justification: RMSE is added alongside R2 for pruning evaluation. Added comparisons introduce block-removal/retraining and two-state Gaussian-HMM settings. The existing contaminated-data evaluation, block length 100 and 3000/1000/1000 pruning split remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The UCR case study gains comparisons with three temporal-attribution methods on the existing anomaly patterns. Label-audit examples lose some comparator and dimension traces. The block-length, stride, model-size, model-choice and least-helpful-pruning analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 independent pruning experiments and retain the same mean-based reporting. v3 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark AUC/F1/runtime entries, UCR example-level F1 scores and RMSE pruning curves. Matched TimeInf benchmark scores remain identical. New comparisons change rankings: on UCR, DCdetector has F1 0.34 versus TimeInf's 0.23, while TimeInf retains higher AUC, 0.79 versus 0.74.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the empirical block distribution to average n-m+1 valid blocks, strengthens convexity to strong convexity and specializes the preliminary contamination definition to point masses. It removes the lag-one contamination example. The core derivation remains, but the added first equality in Equation (4) has a sign inconsistent with Equation (3).

C1.justification: v3 narrows the novelty description from 'unexplored' to 'under-explored' and explicitly positions TimeInf as a unified framework addressing existing temporal-attribution methods. Forecasting usefulness, model agnosticity and annotation-debugging potential were already claimed in v1, although their prominence changes.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving block LOOCV's sample removal, conditional influence's restricted context and LWCV's latent-state assumptions. New limitations acknowledge validation-loss focus, unexplored distribution shifts and marginal gains on high-dimensional data. The label-audit discussion also more strongly attributes poor benchmark scores to unreliable annotations.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 1, task-specific loss and scoring instructions in Appendix H, and implementation settings for the new attribution baselines. Conversely, v1's explicit code-availability statement and repository link disappear; this establishes reduced access information, not that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from v1's discussion of TimeSHAP, KernelSHAP extensions and influence functionals to direct comparisons with regular influence, conditional influence and LWCV. Section 2.1 and the new comparison table substantially develop this relationship, alongside new citations for structured cross-validation and additional anomaly detectors.

P1.justification: The introduction and theoretical narrative are extensively rewritten; Motivation and standalone Related Work are replaced by integrated preliminaries and prior-method discussion. Forecasting and model agnosticity move to appendices, while interpretability, annotation auditing, limitations and task-specific explanations receive dedicated sections.

P2.justification: v3 adds a conceptual comparison table, expands the main benchmark table, redesigns Figure 1 with method groups and F1 annotations, and adds an RMSE row to the pruning figure. Existing annotation-audit figures are cropped and relocated, and numerous retained displays are reorganized within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: Direct temporal-attribution comparisons fill an important evidential gap in v1, while procedural explanations and explicit limitations improve assessability. These gains are qualified by new inconsistencies: the claimed sub-0.65 UCR competitors include DCdetector at 0.74, Figure 7 plots Data Shapley despite its stated exclusion, and Equation (4) introduces a sign mismatch. Together with removal of the code link, these issues limit the net improvement.
